validation_reproduction.verdict: MATCH - evaluate_student refuses to compute test figures otherwise

refit_for_the_new_model: sequence_decode.py   re-selected independently on this model's validation
night_confidence.py  tier boundaries re-fitted on this model's entropy
protocol.note: Every one of these is fitted per-model. Inheriting any of them would describe the previous model.

beats_the_leaky_teacher.note: the inherited teacher trained on 14 of these 15 subjects and is therefore contaminated; the 139K student now exceeds even that

why_this_was_not_automatic.concern: epoch-level metrics improved across the board, but the packet asserts DERIVED metrics, and those moved in both directions.

REM_Latency.why: REM latency is a MINIMUM over the night, so it is monotonically sensitive to REM recall. This model's REM recall rose from 0.755 to 0.799, which necessarily pulls the first predicted REM epoch earlier. A structural property of the metric, not a defect in the model.

Light_Deep_Ratio.why: N3 is over-predicted 1.41x, and N3_Duration is this ratio's denominator

the_deciding_test.question: did any metric the packet is willing to ASSERT become unassertable?
the_deciding_test.answer: No. Every regression is confined to metrics already marked `unreliable`, which the packet already refuses to state without an explicit caveat. Nothing that was safe to assert stopped being safe, and one metric became usable that was not.

false_soremp.note: the narcolepsy red flag is now absent on every held-out night

rem_periods_predicted_mean.note: M0 was near-exact here; this model under-counts. A genuine regression.

safe_to_assert_per_packet.note: unchanged - the promotion of Wake_After_Sleep_Onset moves it from unreliable to fragile, not to robust

flagship_night_regression.why_it_matters: This is the night EVIDENCE_PACKET.md section 4 opens with - the case that forced the schema to carry error bounds at all.
flagship_night_regression.mechanism: The new model calls a SUSTAINED REM run (>=3 epochs) at epoch 93, which the expert scores N1. The decoder's minimum-run rule is designed for isolated single-epoch spray and cannot catch a sustained false run - by construction, not by oversight.
flagship_night_regression.how_close_to_the_red_flag: 18.5 min against a <15 min SOREMP threshold. It did not trip, but by 3.5 minutes.
flagship_night_regression.does_this_reverse_the_promotion: No, on three grounds, all recorded rather than asserted: REM_Latency is tier `unreliable` under BOTH models so the packet never states it without a caveat; aggregate false SOREMP on test improved 1 -> 0; and epoch-level agreement improved by +0.0535 kappa with every class better. But it is the strongest single argument against, and it should be the first thing re-checked if REM precision is ever worked on.
flagship_night_regression.what_it_points_at: A REM PRECISION problem early in the night, created by the higher REM recall (0.755 -> 0.799). A longer decoder L would catch sustained runs but would also mask genuine SOREMPs, which are the thing the metric exists to detect. This needs a REM-precision fix in the model, not a decoder parameter.

what_changed_in_the_packets.provenance: model_parameters now 139,606 and read from the checkpoint rather than hardcoded; model_encoder and model_eeg_scale added
what_changed_in_the_packets.limitations: the caveat 'the raw-waveform pathway contributes nothing to predictions in this model' was TRUE of student_baseline_E0 and is FALSE here - zeroing the EEG changes 71.27% of predictions. It is now derived from the model's eeg_scale rather than hardcoded, so it cannot outlive the model it describes.
what_changed_in_the_packets.decoder: minrun REM L=3, re-selected independently on this model's own validation data rather than inherited. It changes 0.82% of test epochs here against 1.39% for M0 - this model fragments REM less to begin with (1.38x the expert count at argmax, against 2.01x).

open_items: SC4011E0-PSG REM latency error went 18.5 -> 101.0 min. See why_this_was_not_automatic.flagship_night_regression. Highest-priority follow-up if the packet ever needs to assert REM timing.

REM_Periods regressed from near-exact (9.86 vs 9.45) to under-counting (7.52). The decoder's L=3 was selected on this model's validation, but a shorter L may suit a model that fragments less. Worth a sweep against REM_Periods specifically rather than the aggregate objective.

Test ECE got slightly worse under calibration (0.0273 -> 0.0350) while validation improved sharply (0.0557 -> 0.0129). The raw test probabilities were already well calibrated. Worth checking before relying on confidence.
The encoder and N_TOKENS (1 -> 4) changed together and cannot be attributed separately from this run.
EOG is still unused. preprocess_multichannel.py is written and tested but needs the raw EDFs.
